title: Investigating Expectations and Predictive Eye Movements in Humans
author: Garlichs, Lustig, et al.

steps.title: Select initial saccades for analysis
steps.instruction: Decide how many of the earliest saccades per trial will be included (e.g., first and second saccades) and record this choice for downstream statistical tests.

steps.title: Run 2×2 repeated‑measures ANOVA
steps.instruction: Perform a 2 × 2 repeated‑measures ANOVA with the within‑subject factors ‘expectation’ (expected vs. unexpected) and ‘saccade’ (first vs. second) to test whether the proportion of saccades landing in the expected ROI differs from the unexpected ROI.

steps.title: Compute averaged relative frequencies
steps.instruction: Calculate averaged relative frequencies for each participant to control for unequal trial numbers (e.g., expected vs. unexpected facial feature ratio of 1:3), yielding mean percentages for each combination of ‘saccade’ (first, second) and ‘expectation’ (expected, unexpected).

steps.title: Assess order effect – approach 1
steps.instruction: In all trials (match, mismatch, partial) test whether the expected ROI is fixated earliest among the four ROIs.

substeps.instruction: If a trial lacks fixations for some ROIs, assign the missing ROIs random ordinal numbers within that trial.
Compare the distribution of ordinal numbers to a uniform distribution using a subject‑level chi‑square goodness‑of‑fit test (R package ‘htestClust’) and compute Cramer’s V as effect size.
Conduct post‑hoc proportional tests for clustered data, applying correction for the number of tests.
Estimate effect size by averaging subject‑level Cohen’s h.

steps.title: Assess order effect – approach 2
steps.instruction: Separately for partial and mismatch trials, test whether the expected ROI, the unexpected ROI, or the two other ROIs are fixated earlier than the others.

substeps.instruction: Calculate marginal proportion tests for clustered data against binomial distributions, using the random fixation probability based on the number of ROIs (and their area) as the null.
When fixations are missing, assign random numbers; set a reproducible random seed for each participant.

steps.title: Evaluate prior effect on fixation count and duration
steps.instruction: Analyze whether expectations influence the number and dwell time of fixations.

substeps.instruction: If parametric assumptions hold, run paired two‑tailed t‑tests; otherwise use Wilcoxon signed‑rank tests for each participant.
Test whether fixation count and/or dwell time on the expected ROI differ from those on the unexpected ROI and from the average across the other ROIs.
Convert raw counts and dwell times to proportions by dividing fixation numbers by the total number of fixations and dwell times by the total face‑presentation duration.
